title: SIEM 30-Day Review: Orphaned Account and Suspicious Activity

fields.rule: Orphaned Service Account with Outbound Connection and Script Execution
fields.ruleDescription: A service account (svc_nexgen_aodb) used for AODB maintenance was active 5 days ago, initiated an outbound connection to a known VPS provider, and executed a PowerShell script on the AODB server that created a new scheduled task. The account was not removed during off-boarding.
fields.rawEvent:
2026-10-17T02:12:07-05:00 NCIA-SEC-DB01 Windows Event Log 4624: User 'svc_nexgen_aodb' logged on via RDP from external IP 73.189.22.104. [CLIENT: 73.189.22.104]
2026-10-17T02:14:22-05:00 NCIA-SEC-DB01 Windows Event Log 4688: Process 'powershell.exe' created with command line 'powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\AODB\Maintenance\AODB_IndexMaintenance.ps1' by user 'svc_nexgen_aodb'.
2026-10-17T02:15:11-05:00 NCIA-SEC-DB01 Windows Event Log 4624: User 'svc_nexgen_aodb' connected to external host 104.248.52.117 on port 443 (HTTPS). [CLIENT: 10.1.10.20]

instructorNote: This inject confirms the three anomalies from prior injects. The SIEM has all the evidence, but the alerts were not prioritized — a key point for post-exercise discussion on alert tuning and operational noise.
